title: Strategy You Can Test
intro: A goal is not a strategy. Name the obstacle, choose how to beat it, act coherently.

learn.title: The kernel
learn.text:
**Diagnosis:** the critical challenge.
**Guiding policy:** the overall approach. It rules options out.
**Coherent actions:** steps and resources that support each other.

Missing one, it’s a wish, a slogan or a to-do list.

try.q: What does a guiding policy do?
try.explain: A policy that rules nothing out isn’t a policy.

learn.title: Four signs of bad strategy
learn.text:
**Fluff:** buzzwords restating the obvious.
**Not facing the problem:** no named challenge.
**Goals as strategy:** a target with no route.
**Bad objectives:** sprawling lists or unreachable aims.

learn.title: A good example
learn.text:
A chip maker diagnosed it was **losing the performance race.**
Policy: release faster chips at about **three times** the industry pace.
Actions: overlapping teams, heavy simulation, control of its drivers.

try.q: Why do those actions count as coherent?
options: They all serve the same policy
They were planned together in quarterly reviews

learn.title: Ask it of any roadmap
learn.text:
What is the diagnosis?
Which options does the policy rule out?
Do the actions reinforce each other?
Which outcome tells us it’s working, and when do we look?

try.q: A roadmap rules out nothing. What does that suggest?
options: There is no real guiding policy
The strategy is very flexible and ready for change

test.q: What are the three parts of the kernel?
test.explain: Templates of vision and values produce rhetoric, not a diagnosis.
Stripped down, it means being a bank.

test.q: A city plan had 47 strategies and 178 actions. Which sign?
test.explain: A sprawling list isn’t a choice.

options: Choosing is hard, so plans keep every option
Good strategy is too expensive for most companies to produce
test.explain: Avoiding a choice feels safer than making one.

test.q: Where does strategy become testable for a product team?
options: In its outcome and opportunity tree
In the annual budget and its quarterly forecasts
test.explain: The outcome says what should change; the tree shows the bets.

test.q: What is a strategy, in one line?
options: Coherent action backed by an argument
An ambitious target for the year
A list of the planned initiatives for the year ahead
test.explain: It must explain how the obstacle will be beaten.
